prerequisites: The TFG must be defended and evaluated once there is reliable proof that the student has passed all other subjects of the study plan and therefore has all the necessary credits to obtain the Degree, except those corresponding to the TFG itself.

learning_outcomes.text: General presentation: suitability to norms, legibility, writing, spelling, etc.
Logical and coherent structure in the representation of information, ideas and arguments.
Interest of the author's viewpoints, judgments and conclusions.
Quality of the presentation: appropriate use of media, correctness of oral expression, logical structuring, adequacy to available time, etc.
Ability to interest and capture the audience's attention.
Synthesize and integrate the competencies acquired in the studies.

syllabus_topics: Topics within the area of Engineering in which the student has completed their studies, as indicated in the objectives of each qualification.

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring of in-person activities by the academic tutor
Final document presented by the student
Public presentation of the work before the tribunal and subsequent debate

assessment_rules: The final definition of the assessment system for the End-of-Degree Project will comply with the regulations defined in the End-of-Degree Project Regulation of the School of Engineering. Both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations are conducted through a public presentation before a tribunal of three professors from the School. Although the End-of-Degree Project may be part of a joint work, the presentation must be individual, clearly highlighting the particular aspects or contribution of each student to the whole.
